body_html:
20页纸，裁不了任何案子，却想影响所有案子。

9月2日，特朗普政府向纽约南区法院提交了一份20页的法庭陈述（brief），公开支持OpenAI的核心立场：未经授权使用版权材料训练大语言模型，属于合理使用。这起案件由《纽约时报》于2023年12月提起——如今，美国行政分支亲自下场，站到了原告对面。

引用的每一句都有出处

brief引用的背书来自特朗普2025年1月签署的行政令《Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence》。核心论点写得直白：美国有"强烈利益"去继续发展"强劲且有竞争力的人工智能产业"，并"在全球AI使用的实践与规则上树立标准"；另一句更关键——"在对合理使用原则的误解下去约束LLM开发，将扼杀这样的创造与科学进步，同时损害美国的繁荣与经济流动性"。翻译成大白话：版权问题，不许挡AI领导权的路。

分层看：行政站队，司法先例

这份文件的性质必须先说清：它是法庭陈述，不是裁决——写它的人没有管辖权。但行政分支站队的分量在于"风向"：它向法庭、也向所有同类诉讼的当事人，亮明了本届政府的偏好。第二层看司法：Alsup法官此前裁定的Anthropic 15亿美元和解，处罚的是盗版shadow library，而非训练行为本身；迄今为止，AI训练版权的判例总体偏向AI公司。行政偏好叠加司法走向，两条线目前指向同一个方向。

案子里另一根刺，别忽略

不过这场诉讼不只关于法理：2026年7月，《纽约时报》指控OpenAI在诉讼过程中隐藏证据——若这一指控在后续程序中被坐实，再多政府声援也未必扭转具体案件的事实认定。真正值得盯的还有域外效应：纽约南区法院是全球AI版权诉讼的参照系，这里的每一次风向变化，都会被其他法域的律师写进代理意见。一份brief改变不了判决，但它已经改变了辩论的起点。

明天见。
body_html_en:
Twenty pages that decide no case — yet aim to influence all of them.

On September 2, the Trump administration filed a 20-page court brief in the Southern District of New York, openly backing OpenAI's core position: training large language models on copyrighted material without authorization constitutes fair use. The case was brought by The New York Times in December 2023 — now the executive branch itself has stepped in, on the opposite side of the plaintiff.

Every citation has a source

The brief's backing comes from the January 2025 executive order, "Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence." The core argument is blunt: the United States has a "strong interest" in continuing to develop a "robust and competitive artificial intelligence industry" that "sets the standard for the practice and procedure of AI use globally." The sharper line: "Constraining LLM development under a misunderstanding of fair use doctrine would thwart such creative and scientific progress while hindering American prosperity and economic mobility." In plain terms: copyright shall not stand in the way of AI leadership.

Read it in layers: executive alignment, judicial precedent

First, the nature of the document: it is a court brief, not a ruling — its authors hold no jurisdiction. But the weight of the executive branch's alignment lies in the weather it signals: to the court, and to every party in similar litigation, it states this administration's preference. The second layer is judicial: Judge Alsup's approved $1.5 billion Anthropic settlement punished a pirated shadow library, not training itself; to date, AI-training copyright outcomes have broadly favored AI companies. Executive preference plus judicial drift — both lines currently point the same way.

Don't miss the other thorn in this case

Yet this lawsuit is not only about doctrine: in July 2026, The New York Times accused OpenAI of concealing evidence during the litigation — if that accusation is substantiated downstream, no amount of government support guarantees the fact-finding. The extraterritorial effect deserves watching too: the Southern District of New York is the reference frame for AI copyright litigation worldwide, and every shift in its weather gets quoted in briefs across jurisdictions. A brief changes no verdict — but it has already moved the starting point of the argument.

See you tomorrow.

sources.text: 量子位 - 嬴彻科技：卡车自动驾驶运营里程破10亿公里，定义"货运物理AI"

body_html:
10亿公里，够绕地球两万五千圈。

9月3日，嬴彻科技宣布卡车自动驾驶商业运营里程突破10亿公里。这家从干线物流切入的自动驾驶公司，同时完成了一次叙事升级：从"自动驾驶"转向"货运物理AI"（Freight Physical AI），目标是一个覆盖干线、支线/城配与末端的全场景货运机器人网络。按公司口径，它以超90%的份额领跑中国卡车智驾市场，高速网络覆盖率达97%。

10亿公里首先是一份训练资产

对做物理世界AI的公司，里程不是宣传数字，是数据本体。嬴彻把家底拆成三层能力：货运原生智能——Freight World Model货运世界模型，从货车视角生成训练数据；场景智能——ROSL真实世界运营场景库，积累了几十万个高价值场景；运营智能——"运营大脑"云端平台，把单车智能扩展为车队协同。翻译一下：货车遇到的每一次长下坡、加塞、暴雨，都被结构化成可复用的训练素材。物理AI的护城河，不在参数表里，在这种只有运营才能攒出来的东西里。

商业化的证据链

叙事之外，商业化有实据：2026年重卡采购中，多家头部快递公司已将智驾列为100%标配；L4层面，公司获浙江、北京、海南等多地测试牌照，与京东物流开展开放道路L4级干线载货示范应用；5月与顺丰速运、柳汽乘龙实现公开道路无人轻卡商业试运营；海外则在欧洲、日本、中东推进。从高速干线到公开道路无人化，这条线正在加速。

公司口径，怎么读

需要说明：本文数据均为公司官宣口径——90%份额、97%覆盖率都出自发布内容，暂无第三方审计对应。但即便打上折扣，"10亿公里"作为工程事实仍然罕见：它衡量的是系统在真实物流网络里连续运行的年头，而不是封闭场地的演示时长。自动驾驶讲了很多年故事，货运这条线正在用最朴素的方式交卷——公里数。当人形机器人还在赛场上比平衡，货运机器人已经把里程表数到了十亿。物理AI的成熟度，有时候不看发布会，看里程表。

明天见。
body_html_en:
One billion kilometers — enough to circle the Earth 25,000 times.

On September 3, Inceptio announced that its autonomous trucking mileage in commercial operation had crossed 1 billion kilometers. The long-haul-first autonomy company also upgraded its narrative: from "autonomous driving" to "Freight Physical AI," aiming at a full-scenario freight robot network spanning long-haul, regional/urban distribution and last-mile. By company figures, it leads China's autonomous trucking market with over 90% share and 97% highway-network coverage.

A billion kilometers is, first, a training asset

For companies building AI in the physical world, mileage is not a PR number — it is the data itself. Inceptio broke its stack into three layers: freight-native intelligence — a Freight World Model that generates training data from the truck's point of view; scenario intelligence — ROSL, a real-world operations scenario library with hundreds of thousands of high-value scenarios; and operations intelligence — a cloud "operations brain" that scales from single-truck autonomy to fleet coordination. In plain terms: every long downhill, every cut-in, every rainstorm a truck meets gets structured into reusable training material. The moat of physical AI isn't on a spec sheet — it's the kind of thing only operations can accumulate.

The commercialization evidence chain

Beyond narrative, the business has receipts: in 2026 truck procurement, multiple leading couriers made autonomous driving 100% standard; on L4, the company holds test permits across Zhejiang, Beijing, Hainan and more, runs open-road L4 line-haul cargo demonstration with JD Logistics, and in May launched commercial trials of driverless light trucks on public roads with SF Express and Liuzhou Motor; overseas, it is pushing into Europe, Japan and the Middle East. From highway line-haul to open-road driverless, the curve is steepening.

Company figures — how to read them

Full disclosure: every figure here is the company's own — the 90% share and 97% coverage come from its announcement, with no third-party audit behind them. But even discounted, one billion kilometers remains a rare engineering fact: it measures years of continuous operation inside real logistics networks, not demo hours on closed courses. Autonomy has told stories for a decade; freight is turning in its homework the plainest way — odometer readings. While humanoids still compete for balance on stage, freight robots have counted a billion kilometers. For physical AI, maturity sometimes shows up not at keynote events, but on the odometer.

See you tomorrow.
